interface.name: afw_extension
interface.description: Interface returned from afw_extension_initialize() of a loadable extension module. Identifies extension id/version and libafw compile version; additional metadata lives in /afw/_AdaptiveManifest_/<extension_id>. See group afw_included_extensions; example extension srcdirs live outside libafw core (e.g. curl in this base package).

variable.name: extension_id
variable.description: Id of this extension.

variable.name: extension_version
variable.description: Version of this extension.

variable.name: afw_compiled_version
variable.description: Version of libafw this extension was compiled against.

variable.name: afw_compiled_version_hex
variable.description: The hex version of libafw this extension was compiled against.

method.name: initialize
method.description:
This method is called once by afw_environment_load_extension() the first time this instance is loaded in an instance of an Adaptive Framework environment.
This method should call afw_environment register functions and do any other one-time initialization that is required.
After afw_environment_load_extension() calls this function, it will register the instance returned in the AFW environment.

parameter.name: properties
parameter.description: This is the properties supplied to afw_environment_load_extension() or NULL.

parameter.name: p
parameter.description: This is the pool to use for extension resources.

return.description: This is the instance parameter passed or a copy of it with additional private data appended.

method.name: release
method.model_c_code: /* Extension release() is not currently used. */
method.description: Release resources associated with this extension.

interface.name: afw_adapter_factory
interface.description: Factory that creates adapter instances of one adapter type id. Registered with the environment as an adapter_type; conf uses the factory to construct each named adapter. Call afw_adapter_factory_create_adapter_cede_p() (macro) rather than inventing create paths. See group afw_adapter and afwdev add-adapter-type scaffolds for implementers.

variable.description: Type of adapter this factory creates.

variable.name: description
variable.description: Type of adapter this factory creates.

method.description: Create an adapter of the factory's type.

parameter.name: properties
parameter.description: Configuration parameters for the particular type of adapter. This will become the properties object for adapter.

parameter.name: p
parameter.description: The pool that will be used for adapter resources.

return.description: An instance of an adapter.

interface.name: afw_adapter
interface.description: Long-lived pluggable object store (or store-like) instance. Adapters are usually started as services from conf; day-to-day work happens on an afw_adapter_session created from this instance. Prefer helpers in afw_adapter.h over calling destroy / create_adapter_session directly unless you own the lifetime. Method API: afw_adapter_*() macros. Nested session, journal, and index interfaces extend the adapter surface.

variable.name: p
variable.description: Adapter's pool. This pool will exist for the life of the adapter.

variable.name: adapter_id
variable.description: Id of adapter.

variable.name: adapter_type_id
variable.description: Id of adapter type.

variable.name: service_id
variable.description: This is the associated service id. The path of the service is "/afw/_AdaptiveService_/" followed by this id.

variable.name: properties
variable.description: This adapter's properties (configuration) object.

variable.name: source_location
variable.description: This is the source location to help determine how this adapter was defined.

variable.name: trace_flag_id
variable.description: This is the basic trace flag id for this adapter's adapter id.

variable.name: trace_flag_index
variable.description: This is the basic trace flag index for this adapter's adapter id.

variable.name: detail_flag_id
variable.description: This is the detail trace flag id for this adapter's adapter id.

variable.name: detail_flag_index
variable.description: This is the detail trace flag index for this adapter's adapter id.

variable.name: impl
variable.description: Used by adapter common code.

method.name: destroy
method.description:
This method should not be called directly unless you are manually managing the lifetime of this adapter. The functions in afw_adapter.h will call this method when there are no more references to this adapter and then destroy the pool passed to the create function.
The implementation of this method releases any resource not tied to that pool.

method.name: create_adapter_session
method.description: This method should not be called directly unless you are manually managing the lifetime of this adapter. The functions in afw_adapter.h will call this method to create an adapter session instance and will call the session's destroy() method when the session has no more references.

return.description: Pointer to new adapter session instance.

interface.name: afw_adapter_object_type_cache
interface.description: Per-adapter cache of object type definitions used by afw_adapter_get_object_type() and related paths. Speeds repeated type lookups within a session or adapter lifetime. Call methods via afw_adapter_object_type_cache_*() macros. See group afw_adapter.

variable.name: session
variable.description: Associated adapter session.

variable.name: all_object_types_immutable
variable.description:
All object types for associated adapter are immutable.
If true, afw_adapter_get_object_type() will call the set() method when new object types are created.
If false, afw_adapter_get_object_type() will only cache object type for session.

method.description: Get a object type.

parameter.description: Pointer to this adapter object type cache instance.

parameter.name: object_type_id
parameter.description: Object type id of object type to get from cache.

parameter.name: final_result
parameter.description:
Pointer to place to return flag.
If true, afw_adapter_get_object_type() will always return the result of calling the get() method.
If false and get() returns NULL, afw_adapter_get_object_type() will try to create and return a new object_type and return. The set() method will be called if all_object_types_immutable is true.

interface.name: afw_adapter_session
interface.description: Per-use session on an adapter: retrieve/get/add/modify/replace/delete objects, optional transactions, and related journal/index hooks. Sessions are typically short-lived (request or action scope). Prefer afw_adapter.h helpers that create and release sessions with correct reference counting. Call methods via afw_adapter_session_*() macros (e.g. retrieve_objects, get_object).

variable.name: adapter
variable.description: This session's associated adapter.

variable.name: p
variable.description: This session's pool. Exists for the life of the adapter session.

method.name: destroy
method.description:
This method should not be called directly unless you are manually managing the lifetime of this adapter. The functions in afw_adapter.h will call this method when there are no more references to this adapter session.
The implementation releases resources acquired since the session was created by create_adapter_session().

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description: Pointer to this adapter session instance. Make sure to call commit or changes will be lost.

method.name: retrieve_objects
method.description: Retrieve adaptive objects via this adapter that match criteria.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description: Pointer to this adapter session instance.

parameter.name: impl_request
parameter.description: Pass this as first parameter of afw_adapter_impl_request_*() functions. See afw_adapter_impl.h for more information.

parameter.name: object_type_id
parameter.description: The object type of objects to be retrieved.

parameter.name: criteria
parameter.description: Query criteria. Use member filter or normalized, whichever is easier, to filter the objects retrieved. See afw_query_criteria.h for more information. The other members should be ignored.

parameter.name: callback
parameter.description:
Callback function will be called each time an object is retrieved and once with a NULL object pointer when finished.
The callback function will call afw_object_release() on the object when finished with it. If you want to have the object last past the callback, call afw_object_get_reference() on the object before calling the callback.

parameter.name: adapter_type_specific
parameter.description:
This is an adapter type specific object parameter or NULL.
If the adapter type supports this parameter, the object type of the object is available via the afw adapter with an object type id of:
_AdaptiveAdapterTypeSpecific_${adapterType}_retrieve_objects
where ${adapterType} is the adapter type id.

parameter.name: p
parameter.description: Pool used for objects passed to callback.

method.name: get_object
method.description: Retrieve an read-only copy of an adaptive object via adapter.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description: Pointer to this adapter session instance.

parameter.name: impl_request
parameter.description: Pass this as first parameter of afw_adapter_impl_request_*() functions. See afw_adapter_impl.h for more information.

parameter.name: object_type_id
parameter.description: Object type of object to get.

parameter.name: object_id
parameter.description: Object id of object to get.

parameter.name: callback
parameter.description:
Callback function will be called once with either the object retrieved or a NULL object pointer if not found.
The callback function will call afw_object_release() on the object when finished with it. If you want to have the object last past the callback, call afw_object_get_reference() on the object before calling the callback.

parameter.name: adapter_type_specific
parameter.description:
This is an adapter type specific object parameter or NULL.
If the adapter type supports this parameter, the object type of the object is available via the afw adapter with an object type id of:
_AdaptiveAdapterTypeSpecific_${adapterType}_get_object
where ${adapterType} is the adapter type id.

parameter.name: p
parameter.description: Pool used for object passed to callback.

method.name: add_object
method.description: Add an adaptive object via this adapter.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description: Pointer to this adapter session instance.

parameter.name: impl_request
parameter.description: Pass this as first parameter of afw_adapter_impl_request_*() functions. See afw_adapter_impl.h for more information.

parameter.name: object_type_id
parameter.description: Object type of object to add.

parameter.name: suggested_object_id
parameter.description: The suggested object id of the added object. This object id must be unique within the object type. If NULL or at the adapter's option, the adapter will generate a unique object id.

parameter.name: object
parameter.description:
Object to add.
Unless documented otherwise by non-default options, this object only needs to exist for the life of the add_object() call. Some adapters have options that require longer lifetimes for these objects. For example, a memory adapter can be created with the option to not clone an object when added to memory store. In this case, it's the caller responsibility to create the object in a pool that has the minimal lifetime of the memory adapter itself. For instance, the adapter's pool can be used during object create. The memory adapter then uses the object's pool's get_reference() and release() methods to manage the lifetime of the object.

parameter.name: adapter_type_specific
parameter.description:
This is an adapter type specific object parameter or NULL.
If the adapter type supports this parameter, the object type of the object is available via the afw adapter with an object type id of:
_AdaptiveAdapterTypeSpecific_${adapterType}_add_object
where ${adapterType} is the adapter type id.

return.description: Object id of added object.

interface.name: afw_array_setter
interface.description:
Mutable face for an adaptive array used as a growable sequence (vector) and as a double-ended queue (stack/queue). Obtained when the array implementation allows mutation; NULL from get_setter means immutable. Call methods via afw_array_setter_*() macros. Convenience helpers afw_array_*() on the array instance call through get_setter. See group afw_array.
Indexes are afw_integer_t. Non-negative values are zero-based from the start. Negative values count from the end (-1 is the last element for get/set/remove, or insert before the last element for insert). After that adjustment, insert allows index equal to the current count (append); set and remove_value_by_index require a valid existing element index.
End operations: push_value appends (LIFO push / FIFO enqueue); pop_value removes and returns the last value (LIFO pop); shift_value removes and returns the first value (FIFO dequeue). There is no separate unshift method on this interface; use insert_value(instance, 0, value, xctx) to insert at the front (unshift). Content remove_value removes the first equal value (bag-style), not by position.

Remove the last value from the array and return it (pop back / LIFO pop). If the array is empty, returns NULL without error and sets *found to false when found is non-NULL.
Optional found (like object get_property_as_* helpers): pass a pointer to receive whether an element was removed. Pass NULL if the caller does not need that distinction. This matters when a stored value pointer can itself be NULL or undefined: empty is found==false; a removed NULL/undefined slot is found==true with a NULL or undefined return. For typical Adaptive Script use, empty returns NULL which is_nullish / is_undefined treat as undefined (ECMAScript-like empty pop). Prefer found or the return value over get_count() as an empty guard; get_count() can be O(n) on some implementations (memory ring).
When an element is removed, the returned pointer is the value that was stored; it is not cloned. Its lifetime remains that of the value and its pool; the array no longer retains that slot.

Prefer found or the return value over get_count() as an empty guard.
When an element is removed, the returned pointer is the value that was stored; it is not cloned. Its lifetime remains that of the value and its pool; the array no longer retains that slot.

inf_variable.name: is_evaluated_of_data_type
inf_variable.description: Data type of this value when it is already fully evaluated (finished typed layout). NULL if the value is not yet evaluated (IR such as calls, constructs, references). When non-NULL, AFW_VALUE_IS_DATA_TYPE / afw_value_is_* may cast to the matching typed struct. Distinct from data_type (produce type may be known earlier).

method.name: optional_release
method.description: This is an optional method that exists if the value's memory is managed. Constant values that are compiled into object code are not managed.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description: Pointer to this adaptive value instance.

method.name: clone_or_reference
method.description:
If this is a non-managed or permanent value the instance is returned asis. Otherwise, this will return a clone of the instance or instance with its reference count incremented.
There are 3 possible results:
1) If the value is managed and the value's internal value has an get_reference() method, the result of calling the value's internal get_reference() is returned.
2) If the value is managed and the value's internal value does not have an get_reference method, a clone of the value in the supplied pool (p) is returned.
3) If the value is not managed or permanent, the instance is returned asis.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description: Pointer to this adaptive value instance.

return.description: The result as described in the method description.

method.name: create_iterator
method.description: This will return an 'afw_iterator_old' instance or NULL if this value does not support iteration.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description: Pointer to this adaptive value instance.

return.description: This is an new instance of afw_iterator_old.

method.name: optional_evaluate
method.description: This is an optional method used to evaluate an adaptive value. Normally the afw_value_evaluate() macro should be used instead or calling this method directly since it might be NULL.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description: Pointer to this adaptive value instance.

return.description: Evaluated adaptive value.

method.name: get_data_type
method.description:
This method returns the expected data type of the result of calling afw_value_evaluate() on this adaptive value, if available. This is determined at the time the value is created.
For fully evaluated values, the data type will always be available.
For values like 'call', the data type will be available if it can be determined at the value's create time. For instance, if a function always returns a specific data type or if the return data type is polymorphic and the data type of the first parameter can be determined, then the data type will be available.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description: Pointer to this adaptive value instance.

return.description: The data type of the adaptive value or NULL if not available.

method.name: get_evaluated_meta
method.description: This method returns an object value for accessing a value's meta.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description:
Pointer to this adaptive value instance.
IMPORTANT: Do not evaluate instance before calling since meta is harvested from the value's inf.

return.description: The this is an evaluated object value that can be used to access the value's meta.

method.name: get_evaluated_metas
method.description: This method returns an array value of with the result of calling afw_value_get_evaluated_meta() for each entry in a value instance. If this is not a value instance with an iterator, such as object or array, an array value with a single value is returned.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description:
Pointer to this adaptive value instance.
NOTE: Always evaluate instance before calling so that right value inf is used.

return.description: The this is an evaluated array value that can be used to access the value's entry meta.

method.name: produce_compiler_listing
method.description: This produces the compiler listing for a value and calls writer with the result.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description: Pointer to this adaptive value instance.

method.name: decompile
method.description: This decompiles this value to utf-8 and calls writer with the result.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description: Pointer to this adaptive value instance.

method.name: get_info
method.description: Get info about a value.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description: Pointer to this adaptive value instance.

parameter.name: info
parameter.description: Struct that will be filled by this method with info about this value.

interface.name: afw_variable_handler
interface.description: Resolves or supplies variables for a qualifier / context (e.g. custom or request-scoped bags). Used by the qualifier stack and context registration. Call methods via afw_variable_handler_*() macros. See group afw_context and afw_xctx.

method.name: get_variable
method.description: Get a variable's value.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description: Pointer to this adaptive variable handler instance.

return.description: Variable's adaptive value or NULL if not found.

method.name: set_variable
method.description: If this variable handler handles this variable, set its value.

parameter.name: instance
parameter.description: Pointer to this adaptive variable handler instance.

return.description: True if this variable is handled by this variable handler.

interface.name: afw_writer
interface.description: Incremental text/byte writer used when serializing values (JSON and similar). Supports indent/tab for pretty-print; write_raw_cb for callback-style consumers. Prefer writers over building large intermediate strings when streaming. Call methods via afw_writer_*() macros. See group afw_writer.

variable.name: p
variable.description: Pool used for writer resources including write method implementation.

variable.name: write_raw_cb
variable.description: This can be passed to functions that expect an afw_write_cb_t callback. The first parameter passed to the callback must be this afw_writer instance. This is a raw write, so indentation is ignored and the buffer written must be compatible with the afw_writer instance's content.

variable.name: indent
variable.description: The current indent if whitespace is being added.

variable.name: tab
variable.description: If not NULL, whitespace is added as appropriate. Calls to method write_eol will cause \\n to be written. This tab strings is used as needed to produce the appropriate indent. For example, "\\t" can be specified to cause the number of tab characters needed for the current indent.

method.name: release
method.description: Call flush and release resources associated with this writer.

method.name: flush
method.description: This will flush the writer's buffers. The writer implementation will do nothing if it doesn't support this concept.

method.name: write
method.description: Write the specified bytes.

method.name: write_eol
method.description: If white_space is true, write \n then indent next line.

method.name: increment_indent
method.description: If white_space is true, increase indent.

method.name: decrement_indent
method.description: If white_space is true, decrease indent.
